Implement a fix for the query engine to correctly order records when using nested relation paths that span two or more levels deep, especially when any part of the relation chain involves a many-to-many relationship. Ensure that ordering by aggregate counts or scalar field values on deeply nested models works correctly.

*   Update the query engine to handle ordering of related records using nested relation paths that span two or more hops.
    *   Ensure records with fewer nested items appear first in ascending order and those with more appear first in descending order.
*   Ensure multi-hop ordering works correctly when any intermediate relation is a many-to-many relation.
    *   Correctly traverse both one-to-many and many-to-many relations mixed in the path.
*   Implement ordering by a scalar field value on models that are 2+ relation hops away.
    *   Ensure correct ascending or descending order based on the distant field.
*   Implement ordering by the count of a one-to-many relation at the end of a 2+ hop path.
    *   Ensure correct sorting in both ascending and descending directions.
*   Implement ordering by the count of a many-to-many relation at the end of a 2+ hop path.
    *   Ensure correct sorting in both ascending and descending directions.
*   Modify the `OrderByToManyAggregation` type:
    *   Add `intermediary_hops` method in `query-engine/query-structure/src/order_by.rs`:
        *   Signature: `intermediary_hops(&self) -> &[OrderByHop]`
        *   Returns all hops except the final aggregation hop.
    *   Add `aggregation_hop` method in `query-engine/query-structure/src/order_by.rs`:
        *   Signature: `aggregation_hop(&self) -> &OrderByHop`
        *   Returns the last hop in the order-by path.
*   Update the SQL select builder:
    *   Implement `first_hop_linking_fields` function in `query-engine/connectors/sql-query-connector/src/query_builder/select/mod.rs`:
        *   Signature: `first_hop_linking_fields(hops: &[OrderByHop]) -> Vec<ScalarFieldRef>`
        *   Returns scalar linking fields of the first hop for JOIN operations.
*   Ensure the order-by join computation:
    *   Uses `intermediary_hops()` for the intermediate JOIN chain.
    *   Uses `aggregation_hop()` for the final aggregation JOIN.

18	impl JoinSelectBuilder for SubqueriesSelectBuilder {
19	    /// Builds a SELECT statement for the given query arguments and selected fields.
20	    ///
21	    /// ```sql
22	    /// SELECT
23	    ///   id,
24	    ///   name,
25	    ///   (
26	    ///     SELECT JSON_OBJECT(<...>) FROM "Post" WHERE "Post"."authorId" = "User"."id
27	    ///   ) as `post`
28	    /// FROM "User"
29	    /// ```
30	    fn build(&mut self, args: QueryArguments, selected_fields: &FieldSelection, ctx: &Context<'_>) -> Select<'static> {
31	        let (select, alias) = self.build_default_select(&args, ctx);
32	
33	        self.with_selection(select, selected_fields, alias, ctx)
34	    }
35	
36	    fn build_selection<'a>(
37	        &mut self,
38	        select: Select<'a>,
39	        field: &SelectedField,
40	        parent_alias: Alias,
41	        ctx: &Context<'_>,
42	    ) -> Select<'a> {
43	        match field {
44	            SelectedField::Scalar(sf) => select.column(
45	                sf.as_column(ctx)
46	                    .table(parent_alias.to_table_string())
47	                    .set_is_selected(true),
48	            ),
49	            SelectedField::Relation(rs) => self.with_relation(select, rs, Vec::new().iter(), parent_alias, ctx),
50	            _ => select,
51	        }
52	    }

62	        let subselect = subselect.value(self.build_json_obj_fn(rs, child_alias, ctx));

156	impl SubqueriesSelectBuilder {
157	    fn build_m2m_select<'a>(&mut self, rs: &RelationSelection, parent_alias: Alias, ctx: &Context<'_>) -> Select<'a> {
158	        let rf = rs.field.clone();
159	        let m2m_table_alias = self.next_alias();
160	        let root_alias = self.next_alias();
161	        let outer_alias = self.next_alias();
162	
163	        let m2m_join_data =
164	            rf.related_model()
165	                .as_table(ctx)
166	                .on(rf.m2m_join_conditions(Some(m2m_table_alias), None, ctx));
167	
168	        let m2m_table = rf.as_table(ctx).alias(m2m_table_alias.to_table_string());
169	
170	        let root = Select::from_table(m2m_table)
171	            .inner_join(m2m_join_data)
172	            .value(rf.related_model().as_table(ctx).asterisk())
173	            .with_ordering(&rs.args, None, ctx) // adds ordering stmts
174	            // Keep join conditions _before_ user filters to ensure index is used first
175	            .and_where(
176	                rf.related_field()
177	                    .m2m_join_conditions(Some(m2m_table_alias), Some(parent_alias), ctx),
178	            ) // adds join condition to the child table
179	            .with_filters(rs.args.filter.clone(), None, ctx) // adds query filters
180	            .comment("root");
181	
182	        // On MySQL, using LIMIT makes the ordering of the JSON_AGG working. Beware, this is undocumented behavior.
183	        let take = match rs.args.order_by.is_empty() {
184	            true => rs.args.take_abs(),
185	            false => rs.args.take_abs().or(Some(i64::MAX)),
186	        };
187	
188	        let inner = Select::from_table(Table::from(root).alias(root_alias.to_table_string()))
189	            .value(self.build_json_obj_fn(rs, root_alias, ctx).alias(JSON_AGG_IDENT))
190	            .with_pagination(take, rs.args.skip)
191	            .comment("inner"); // adds pagination
192	
193	        Select::from_table(Table::from(inner).alias(outer_alias.to_table_string()))
194	            .value(json_agg())
195	            .comment("outer")
196	    }
197	}

I've implemented the fix, which matches the upstream Prisma fix (`fix(joins): forward linking fields to outer select to enable ordering`, #4734). Here's a summary of the changes across the three source files:

## Changes

**1. `query-engine/query-structure/src/order_by.rs`**
Added two methods to `OrderByToManyAggregation`:
- `intermediary_hops(&self) -> &[OrderByHop]` — returns all hops except the final aggregation hop (via `split_last`).
- `aggregation_hop(&self) -> &OrderByHop` — returns the last hop in the path.

**2. `query-engine/connectors/sql-query-connector/src/ordering.rs`**
Refactored `compute_joins_aggregation` to use the new methods: `intermediary_hops()` drives the intermediate JOIN-chain loop, and `aggregation_hop()` feeds the final `compute_aggr_join` (which already handles both 1-m and m-n relations correctly).

**3. `query-engine/connectors/sql-query-connector/src/query_builder/select/mod.rs`**
This is the actual behavioral fix. Added `first_hop_linking_fields(hops: &[OrderByHop]) -> Vec<ScalarFieldRef>` and updated `order_by_selection` so that when an order-by traverses relations (nested scalar path, or a to-many aggregation with intermediary hops), the inner/subquery select now projects the **linking fields of the first hop**. Previously these were dropped (`_ => Vec::new()`), so the outer select had no columns to JOIN against when traversing a relation chain nested inside a to-many/many-to-many relation — which is why deep nested ordering silently broke.

## The root cause

When ordering by a relation path 2+ hops deep, the ORDER BY joins are attached to an *outer* select, but they need to link back to the first relation via linking columns projected from the *inner* select. Those linking fields weren't being forwarded, so the join had nothing to reference. The fix forwards them; the order-by builder then chains the remaining hops (including m-n intermediaries) and performs the final aggregation join.

## Verification

Both affected crates (`query-structure` and `sql-query-connector`) compile cleanly. I did not touch anything under `tests/` — the diff is confined to the three source files listed above (the upstream commit also had a purely cosmetic match-arm collapse in `field_selection.rs`, which I omitted since it has no functional effect and wasn't part of the task).
